title: A polynomial rule for directed walls with choices
claim: For the six directed placements (allowed places {0, 2}: 54, 62, 110, 147, 155, 203), whether an odd class contradicts is decidable in time polynomial in L M and the bit length of the class. Walls are monotone paths whose moves are allowed one at a time; good walls are those strictly above or strictly below their copy, and they are closed under pointwise maximum and minimum; Aubry's ordered maximum and a split at a repeated square yield a good wall that is simple on the type-preserving cover, so simple cycles of the wall graph suffice on every torus; for each period up to the size of that cover a max-closed constraint problem, decided by arc consistency, finds a good wall. Among the twelve bending placements only the four honeycomb ones with a free place (111, 125, 159, 215) lack a known polynomial rule.
failure_conditions: A configuration where the decider and the ground truth (simple cycles on 3 x 3 and 3 x 4, the own solver on covers and strips on larger tori) disagree.
A wall reduced by the ordered maximum and the split that stops being valid or good, or that ends with a repeated square of the type-preserving cover.
foundation_claim_scope: Twisted fair worlds on triangular tori with cylinder covers; exact statements and finite computations. Lattices are declared; no space or physics is claimed.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library, with the wall graph and own solver of WALLS-WITH-CHOICES-20261024-001A-P001) verifies the directed structure on 360 configurations, shortens 245 random and five listed crossing walls to good walls simple on the type-preserving cover, and finds the decider equal to the ground truth on 1432 classes on 3 x 3 to 4 x 5; three controls. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with computational checks
